task.description: WF-02 Step 3 (test design) for REQ-034 on branch feature/WF02-REQ-034. REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER both PASSED. Scope test: real, testable surface exists (domain decision function, transactional write, composed Telegram reply, /my rendering) -- full Step 3 procedure applies. Per decisions/0006, TEST-DESIGNER writes runnable vitest code for bot logic, not a manual checklist -- this run wrote real test cases into the actual test files rather than only a markdown checklist.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: registering for requires_approval=true, requires_invite=false creates exactly one registrations row with admission='requested'.
AC2: the confirmation states a decision will follow and by when, matching registration_closes_at in the chapter's timezone; the NULL case exercises the stated fallback.
AC3: a second request yields the person's CURRENT pending status, exactly one row remains.
AC4: a request succeeds even when the event's admitted count already equals capacity (admission='requested', never 'waitlisted' or a refusal).
AC5: qr_token IS NULL on the created row, and /my shows it with pending state and NO QR image.
AC6: creating a request writes exactly one audit_log row naming actor/action/entity/entity_id.
AC7: an event with requires_approval=false is unaffected (still admits/waitlists per REQ-020/021).

result.summary: Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-034.md mapping every one of the 7 acceptance criteria to concrete, already-committed vitest cases, plus the actual test code itself (per decisions/0006-test-framework-vitest.md, which supersedes WF-02 Step 3's stale 'manual checklist' text -- a docs/agents/decisions/ record is never overridden by a workflow step per core-directives.md's precedence rules). No new test file was created; new cases were added to the two files BACKEND-DEV already touched (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.test.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts) plus two further files whose existing infrastructure is the only correct place to verify handler-level/rendering ACs that domain-level tests structurally cannot reach (apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.test.ts for AC2's composed reply text and AC3's full-dispatch double-tap; apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts, extending its existing REQ-024 AC3/AC4/AC5 QR-gating test in place with a 'requested' fixture row, for AC5's actual /my rendering). tg_id discipline: grepped every existing test file's nextTgId/tgSeq literal first (highest claimed band: handlers/staff.test.ts's 1_010_000_000, ISS-0020). No new tg_id range is claimed or needed -- every new case calls an existing, already-present, self-incrementing counter local to the file it was added to (no new hardcoded tg_id literal appears anywhere in this diff). AC1: new DB-level case in registration.db.test.ts reads the persisted row back directly (exactly one row, admission='requested', qr_token NULL) -- the existing case BACKEND-DEV updated only asserted on the returned outcome, not the row. AC2: two new full-grammY-dispatch cases in handlers/registration.test.ts, one with registration_closes_at set (asserts the exact chapter-local formatDateTimeInTimezone rendering appears, fallback string absent) and one with it NULL (asserts the fixed fallback string appears, the decision-by prefix is absent, and no null/undefined/Invalid Date leaks into the composed text) -- this is the NULL-fallback exercise the AC explicitly requires and BACKEND-DEV's existing tests never constructed. AC3: one new DB-level case (second registerForEvent call returns already-registered/requested, exactly one row) plus one new handler-level case (the same tgId taps Register twice through two real bot.handleUpdate calls; second reply contains the actual rendered statusRequested label, not just the outcome kind). AC4 (the case this run's task explicitly flagged as most important): two new pure-decision boundary cases in registration.test.ts (seatsLeft 0 and -3, both still requested) PLUS one new real-DB-fixture case in registration.db.test.ts that directly inserts an 'admitted' filler row to genuinely put a requires_approval=true event at capacity 1 (registerForEvent itself cannot produce 'admitted' on this path, so a direct insert is the only way to construct this precondition -- matching this file's existing insertWaitlisted-style convention) with a fixture-sanity assertion before the real one, then confirms a fresh requester still gets 'requested', never 'waitlisted' or a refusal. AC5: the row-level half is covered by AC1's new case (qrToken null); the /my-rendering half required extending handlers/my.test.ts's existing QR-gating test with a fifth 'requested' registration row and updated send-count assertions (6 sends/1 photo/4 text, was 5/1/3), plus a new assertion that the requested row's own text send carries statusRequested and no photo. AC6: new describe block in registration.db.test.ts counting audit_log rows before/after, asserting the row filtered by entityId=registrationId has length exactly 1 with action='registration.request', entity='registration', actorUserId=userId. AC7: no new case written -- would be busywork duplicating existing, unmodified, already-passing coverage (registration.db.test.ts's admitted/waitlisted qr_token-issuance pair, registration.test.ts's row-7/row-8 pure-decision tests, all with requiresApproval defaulting to false and untouched by this diff) -- spec cites these by exact file/describe/it name instead and requires TEST-RUNNER to actually re-run them as part of Step 4's full npm test invocation rather than accepting the prior report as current evidence. Per test-designer.md's own forbidden list ('Don't run the checks yourself'), this run did NOT execute npm test/lint/build itself -- the code was written carefully against the exact existing patterns/imports/field names in each file (verified column/type names directly against apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts and each file's own existing helpers before writing), but actual pass/fail is TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 to establish.
